title: MEN'S BASKETBALL | Chris Jans Media Session - 11/19/26
text: A few things as we get started here today. Um, first and foremost, wear your credentials that your season credentials that you were issued if you're going down to Jackson. Uh, so you don't need that. I will send out an email later today with more information about parking, etc., and those type of logistics. Also to let you all know, we'll honor Josh Hubard with a commemorative game ball for his 2,000th point uh before the game um here uh on uh Friday. Uh coach, we'll make an opening statement today uh and then we'll take questions. Go ahead, coach. >> Yeah, I'd like to uh uh personally give my condolences to uh Jiren Barry and the Bob Barry family back in Debuke, Iowa. Uh, Coach Bob Barry was a young mentor of mine. Uh, he was the football coach, athletic director at my alma mater, Loris College. And I've known him since I was 17 years old. And I didn't play for him, nor did I work for him, but he had a huge impact on my life. um from the time I met him till um this summer when my wife and I Sherry were able to spend um a few hours with him and his wife as he uh battled an illness for some quite some time and he passed a couple days ago and he meant a lot to uh the debut community and to the Loris College community. He's someone that was very very very well respected and loved and um he's certainly going to be missed. Uh on a positive note, I' I'd like to uh congratulate Coach Obi uh and the women's soccer team uh the year that they're having. Certainly uh getting to host an NCA tournament game at home is is is quite the thrill. And then certainly uh Julie Dardy Dennis and uh the volleyball team and heading into uh the SEC tournament. So I want to wish them both well and good luck and I'll open up to questions. We'll start uh to coach's left with Danny P. then we'll go to the second row and Kellen. Let's >> just talk about getting Kamani and Josh down to Jackson play in front of their their fan, you know, the fans and family and all that. And just how you know was the schedule in that game kind of the reason behind that. >> I guess Kamani's uh lucky benefactor. Uh this was more for two reasons. One, as you know, we've spread this game around and I love doing it. We've played in South Haven, Memphis, Tupelo, Jackson since we've been here. And it's important to me to try to do that and try to get to different corners of the state and kind of bring the game to some of our Bulldog fans and the ones that do travel, make it easier for them uh occasionally. Uh but when we scheduled this game and certainly as you know, we do this in advance. Uh it was two reasons. what I just stated, but also with Josh being a senior, thought this would be kind of cool for him to be able to play in his hometown in his senior season and certainly with the landscape changing and the five for five being in place, who knows if this will be his last time playing in in that area of the country. But, um, I'd imagine they're excited. Uh the great thing for me as a coach is you're always worried about distractions and with their personalities, the way they carry themselves, uh you know, it won't affect their play. Um so it's awesome that uh we're able to do that and certainly as Matt mentioned, you know, honoring Josh uh w with this 2000 point deal and being able to do it in front of his hometown and and more family and friends than maybe normal um is quite the treat as well. Go ahead, Kellen, and then we'll get it over to Jacob. >> What do you think it means to Josh and Kamani to be able to go back down uh to their home area and play in front of that crowd again? >> Yeah, I'd imagine on a personal level, it's uh pretty cool, you know? Uh it hearkens me back to when I got the job and all I heard about was Josh Hubard when I got the job. I didn't know Josh Huard when I was coaching at New Mexico State. And one of the first orders of business for for myself and coach Anoir was to drive down to that area and meet the family and Josh and um you know start the recruiting process for him. And at the same time Kamani Hamilton was a young man that had signed with the program prior to my arrival was a year older than Josh and also made a trip down there to spend time with uh Kamani and his family. I still remember um you know the conversation and how it went. how it went. And you know, with Tang being his father and being such a great player, I think it's a cool story that he's back here. He's starting for the Bulldogs where he grew up wanting to play for like his dad did. And, you know, it's it's quite a circle that's brought him back here. So, um I'd imagine they're both got a little extra bounce in their step, uh heading into practice this afternoon before we bust on down there and get ready to play tomorrow night. >> Jacob to coaches, right? and then we'll get to Sam in the second round middle. >> What have you seen from Tulsa and what kind of challenge will they will they present for you guys tomorrow? >> Yeah, Tulsa's led by Eric Conl who I've known for a long time, a very respected coach in our industry, for being a good teacher, for running great programs, for being wellprepared. They're a team that I'm familiar with, a coach I'm familiar with, and they don't beat themselves. They're very well prepared. They'll have a great game plan. Um, they're going to try to take away our weaknesses. They're going to target certain players and they run their offense with great pace and they know what they're trying to do. They're coming off an great season where they broke records. They won 30 games. They finished in the finals of the NIT tournament. Um, and obviously, uh, they've got great momentum this year. They're undefeated. They're 4-0. So for for me, like always, one of the challenges is to make sure our guys understand, yeah, coming off a great exhilarating road win against a power five team. You know, now we have to play a team that's not in the power five. Certainly as coaches, you know, it's not a lack of respect at all. And we're going to we're prepared just as hard as we did for that game as we are for this one. But sometimes young people um you know, can get it mixed up in their brain about who they're playing and maybe not prepared quite as well or hard or look at them differently. And so that'll be part of the challenge and certainly uh we've already begun trying to do that. >> Sam, >> when it comes to Tristan Reed's following, what can you do as a coach to prevent, you know, players from getting into follow trouble, especially a younger player like him who's new to the college game? >> Yeah, it's not just Tristan. Certainly, he's a big part of it. I think our team in general is following too much. You know, our our free throw rate defensively is poor. You know, I want to be an aggressive I want to have an aggressive style of play, but that's always a fine line. And I think it's a couple different reasons why. One, I think the officials call the games closer at the beginning of the year, tighter, and I thought the officials the other night were very consistent. Uh they they called a tight game. It wasn't didn't feel like an SEC game. And those guys are high level officials, all three of them. And but they were very consistent with how they called the game. and we didn't adjust to it, you know, as players, as coaches, um, as well as, you know, we would have liked looking back. Um, but we've just got to be more disciplined. We got what we try to use around our program is trust the technique of how we guard the ball and where we position our hands and our feet. And then certainly in closeout techniques or at the rim plays where shielding has been very popular and something we work on every single day. So, a lot of different things, a lot of different techniques, and getting those guys to, you know, buy into the techniques that we're trying to install since they've arrived in June. And and a lot of them are doing it, but now they're not transferring it to live play, and that's what's most important. So, we're going to continue to harp on them. We're going to try to devise new drills, new ways. Certainly, film uh and learning from our mistakes uh is big. And then specifically to Tristan, um he's a valuable part of this year's team. I don't care how old he is. I don't care what is beside Christian Reed number 33, what uh initials are there. He's got to have a big impact for us and he did Tuesday and we've been waiting for it and he's got to do it every single night and he can't do it when he's saddled with foul problems. So, um I think he's got all the tools to be an excellent defender. He's got length. Uh he's a great kid. He plays hard. He's bouncy. He's got girth. Uh he's got feel. uh he just gota uh continue to trust the techniques and and not put himself in harm's way. >> We got time for a few more before coach has to get to practice. We'll go to Colin Front row middle. Kind of adding off of that, this is more of a a retrospective thing. Obviously, you don't want to get in those situations in the moment, but what did you maybe learn about your team in terms of dealing with foul trouble and the depth of the roster and being able to pick up after each other? You know, I think being able to play um 11 and even 12 guys one game those first three games of the season was huge that way. Not just giving everyone tape and minutes for us and for them individually, but also giving them some confidence and giving us some confidence that we can handle a foul situation and an ankle. Knock on wood. Um because it's going to happen. It ain't the first time we're going to have people saddled with fouls. And then it allows you to make decisions. Are you gonna place certain players with two in the first half, which is becoming more uh in vogue than it maybe was in the old school yester year. Um but I think again playing those games the way we did and having some opportunities um to play guys even in the Xavier game, you know, playing Jaylen Collingwood and Willie Bunette um a ton of minutes down the stretch to get them more prepared for um future games. um even though it was in a losing cause, um hopefully it'll um help us uh going forward that way. >> Y'all have signed four high school prospects since the last time we talked to you. Just talk about what each of those guys will bring to the table and what you saw in their game. >> Yeah, we've signed four uh high school guys. Um obviously Jack Mitchell is a lightning fast point guard from Tulsa, Oklahoma. He was the first verbally uh verbal commit we had and um he's I haven't coached him yet, but I think once we get our eyes on him and our hands on him, um he'll be the fastest point guard that I've ever coached with the ball. At least that's our expectation um that way. And um he's got a lot of ability and guys that are built like that usually don't shoot the ball um um very well, but but he shoots it pretty good walking in the door. So, we're certainly excited um about him. Um Jaylen White um is a is a wing from uh the Vegas area that plays at Bella Vista uh which is a very respected program in the Phoenix area. Uh plays for a guy that's had great players in Mike George and um Jaylen is a dynamic player that's got huge upside. He's got great length, great uh physical ability. He's a big- time jumper. He can make shots. um you know, his best basketball is definitely ahead of him and he's uh also a wonderful kid. We're excited obviously about all four of them. We wouldn't have signed him. Um Chris Brown u ironically plays in Phoenix as well. Um but he is originally from the Bahamas and he's uh very um uh in a positive way for us. Um his his size and length is very unique. you know, he's 69, but he's got like a 77 wingspan, which is freakish um that way. And for us, that's a big deal. The wingspans and the lengths and their reach are more important than how tall they are, how long their neck is or their torso is, in my opinion, doesn't help on the basketball court as much as the length of of their uh limbs, if you will. Um helps them on the court. And and he's got great IQ. He knows how to play. He's got a good skill level. uh you know, I think he has a chance to to walk in and because of the length, because of the skill level, because of the feel, have a chance to impact us that way. And then the most recent one, um Bryson Hammermeister, um is a Florida kid from the Fort Meyers area that caught our eye this summer. Um and he was a little under the radar, uh because of some injuries and moving around, but he's a hard playing um guy that again, another another wing that can move around. Uh the last two years we've really tried to recruit guys that are more positionless and can play multiple positions and Bryson can really shoot the ball. Uh he kind of shoots it like Willie does kind of behind his head a little bit that way which makes it harder to get to to contest and he can get his shot off against pretty much anybody that way and he's a really really hard playing kid. So the theme for us in our last two classes have been just guys that are quality human beings, guys that possess um the right mindset in terms of being about the right stuff in our opinion of working hard, having the right approach every single day from the diligence that we've done. Um so we're certainly excited about the three freshman that we had this year and um we're as excited as you can be about not coaching a group of young people of what we think they are on paper as well. >> Go ahead, Sam. and wrap us up >> with King going 14 for 14 at the line last game. Just first, was he a player on your team you would have predicted to go 14 for 14 in a game? And also, how much was that something he worked on in the offseason? >> You'd have to ask him about what he's working on, you know, when I'm not around. You know, I know what we do when we're around and we're legally allowed to be with him and work on his game. Um, you know, I think more importantly, um, in the that game, it's like anything, it becomes contagious and when you start making it, you know, the rim gets bigger, you know, for us down the stretch to run a play for him um to either get fouled or scored when the game was in in the balance and then do it again on a side out situation when it was really really crucial as the game clock was I think at 12. um speaks to our confidence that we had in him in that particular night. I can't imagine that, you know, his confidence isn't through the roof right now. He made a huge three right in front of our bench that RJ and Hub set up for him with the dribble penetration that they both had leading up to the catch and shoot opportunity that King benefited from. But, um he's in a really good place. You know, he's playing very very well. Um you know, King's hard to guard. um you know, he's he's just he's unpredictable a little bit. Um which can be frustrating as a coach, but like playing against that is probably no fun. Um you don't know exactly what he's going to do at times and he's full throttle. You know, he's he's playing head down. Um and and obviously as a coach, you get a little nervous sometimes, but um in that particular game, it was really really good for him and for us. >> Thank you guys. We'll see you Friday in Jackson. If not, we'll see you November 30th for our next media session. >> Thanks, guys. Thanks.
